This will likely contribute to increasing rates of problem gambling in the years to come,” Nower added.The Associated Press contributed reportingExplore more on these topicsNew YorkPrediction marketsLetitia JamesKathy HochulLaw (US)GamblingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Arsenal’s title defence: keeping tired players fit and the Vinícius question | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Key players have piled up extra minutes at the World Cup and signing Vinícius Júnior would smash their wage structure
Author: Andrew Beasley
Headline: Key players have piled up extra minutes at the World Cup and signing Vinícius Júnior would smash their wage structure
Content: Gabriel Magalhães has played 4,210 minutes since the start of last season, and is one of several Arsenal players who have had heavy workloads.Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/GettyView image in fullscreenGabriel Magalhães has played 4,210 minutes since the start of last season, and is one of several Arsenal players who have had heavy workloads.Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/GettyArsenalArsenal’s title defence: keeping tired players fit and the Vinícius questionKey players have piled up extra minutes at the World Cup and signing Vinícius Júnior would smash their wage structureAndrew BeasleyFri 31 Jul 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAfter beating MK Dons 3-0 in a training-ground friendly last weekend,Arsenaltruly begin their pre-season programme against Girona on Saturday evening. It marks a return to action for the Premier League champions, who will want to show their success last season was not a one-off.Retaining the English title is incredibly difficult if you are not Manchester City. No other club has done it since Manchester United won three in succession from 2007 to 2009. Chelsea have done it once, Liverpool have not managed it for more than 40 years, and it is the best part of a century since Arsenal retained the crown. Mikel Arteta faces a sizeable challenge.Reaching a second successive Champions League final will not be simple either. Manchester City in 2021-22 are the only one of England’s previous five finalists who made it as far as the semi-finals the next season. With the Premier League stronger than ever, competing on two fronts has never been tougher. Transfer business may improve Arsenal’s chances, though their spending has been modest to this point. More than half of the £79m spent was on making Piero Hincapié’s loan permanent.Elsewhere Arsenal have replaced Leandro Trossard with Christos Tzolis, a Greek winger, from Club Brugge. Seven years younger than the Belgian, his arrival is a logical move in future-proofing the squad. However, the left side of Arsenal’s attack would be elevated to truly elite level if they could secure reported target Vinícius Júnior. The on-field argument speaks for itself. Vinícius made 92 carries of at least five metres that ended with him either taking a shot (49) or creating a chance (43) last season, the most of anyone in Europe’s top five leagues. Open-play threat, for a side that has often relied on set pieces, would be considerably increased.Those holding the purse strings at Arsenal may have pause for thought. Capology’s wage data estimates that Vinícius is the joint-third highest paid player in Europe’s top five leagues, earning in excess of £100,000 a week more than anyone at his potential new club. Would Arsenal be willing to rewrite their wage structure? They should expect calls from the agents of their current players if they are. In this sense, Bradley Barcola, with whom they have also been linked, makes a more plausible target. The issue there would be competition fromLiverpool, who are in far greater need of wingers.Chart comparing Vinícius Júnior’s salary with Arsenal’s top paid playersThis is the test facing Andrea Berta, Arsenal’s sporting director. Improving a squad that is already one of the best around is not easy. WhenBerta’s arrived last year, the club’s primary targets were said to be Alexander Isak and Benjamin Sesko, both of whom joined rivals instead. The pool of players who could add something significant to Arteta’s options is drying up.Keeping existing players fit may be more beneficial than enhancing the squad. Arsenal did well to win the league given only a handful of clubs had players that missed more games. Kai Havertz was reportedly their top earner beforeBukayo Saka signed a contract extensionin February, but he only started seven league games. The captain, Martin Ødegaard, was also unavailable for spells, meaning he and Saka started only 10 Premier League matches together in 2025-26. One of them coincided with the only game for which Declan Rice was injured (the 4-1 home win over Aston Villa), another (another home win, 2-1 against Brighton) when he started at right-back.View image in fullscreenMikel Arteta indulges in a bit of training-ground banter with first-team coach Miguel Molina in Girona.Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesThis meant Arteta was rarely able to give key men a breather. Arsenal have five of the Premier League’s top 20 players for club minutes in all competitions since the start of last season. Granted, the goalkeeper David Raya is one of them. But their outfield players with more than 4,200 minutes were Rice (4,456 minutes, the 11th most for a Premier League club), Martín Zubimendi (4,298, 15th), William Saliba (4,254, 17th) and Gabriel Magalhães (4,210, 19th), all vital components of the side’s spine.Saliba also played 795 minutes for France, pushing him past 5,000 minutes before his World Cup was prematurely ended by a back injury that looks likely to sideline him for some time. It is remarkable Rice was able to play 1,026 minutes for England on top of his Arsenal commitments, not least as he hasmanaged nerve pain in a hamstring throughout 2026.This workload clearly impacted his ability to contribute at his best for Thomas Tuchel this summer, and that will be a concern for Arteta. With Viktor Gyökeres also clocking up plenty of playing time for Sweden, Arsenal have six players with at least 4,400 minutes for club and country since the start of last August.Chart showing Arsenal’s players with the most minutes for club and country since 1 August 2025This may have been a factor in Arsenal opting for a relatively low-key pre-season. They visited Asia last summer, but the trip to Catalonia to play Girona is the furthest they will travel this year. Arsenal also have games in Dublin (against Real Betis) and Cardiff (the Community Shield against City) sandwiching home friendlies against Borussia Dortmund and Como.With players still recovering from their World Cup exertions, it may be some time before we see the true Arsenal. A combination of fatigue, injuries and potential squad additions means the process could take far longer than would be ideal.Explore more on these topicsArsenalfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Inter make new approach to Liverpool for Curtis Jones with £30m offer likely | Liverpool | The Guardian

Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Inter have made another approach for Curtis Jones and are willing to raise their offer for the Liverpool midfielder to €35m
Content: Curtis Jones could be nearing his Liverpool exit this summer.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenCurtis Jones could be nearing his Liverpool exit this summer.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersLiverpoolInter make new approach to Liverpool for Curtis Jones with £30m offer likelyItalian champions willing to raise offer for midfielderJones only has one year remaining on contract at AnfieldAndy Hunterin ChicagoFri 31 Jul 2026 14.01 EDTLast modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 20.48 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleInter have made another approach for Curtis Jones and are willing to raise their offer for theLiverpoolmidfielder to €35m (£30m). The Italian champions had a €25m bid for the 25-year-old rejected in June by Liverpool, who value their homegrown player at closer to €40m.Quick GuideBellingham watches Birmingham beat Barça in friendlyShowJude Bellingham returned to St Andrew's as a spectator to see Birmingham City beat Barcelona on penalties in a pre-season friendly. He was also involved in a row with Dominik Szoboszlai afterWednesday’s win over Wrexhamin New York, seemingly over not being handed the captain’s armband when Szoboszlai was substituted during the second half of the friendly.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe new Liverpool head coach, Andoni Iraola, has spoken of the importance of keeping Jones and a local identity at the start of his first season in charge but Inter’s determination to sign the England international, along with the prospect of losing him for free next summer, may well test that resolve.Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolInternazionaleTransfer windownewsShareReuse this content

title: Aasgaard strikes as Rangers start McInnes era with draw at Dundee United | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Thelo Aasgaard earned Derek McInnes his first point as Rangers manager as they fought back for a 1-1 draw against Dundee United
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Thelo Aasgaard earned Derek McInnes his first point as Rangers manager as they fought back for a 1-1 draw against Dundee United
Content: Thelo Aasgaard rescued Rangers and Derek McInnes in a 1-1 draw at Dundee United.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAView image in fullscreenThelo Aasgaard rescued Rangers and Derek McInnes in a 1-1 draw at Dundee United.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAScottish PremiershipAasgaard strikes as Rangers start McInnes era with draw at Dundee UnitedPA MediaFri 31 Jul 2026 17.58 EDTLast modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 20.48 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThelo Aasgaard earned Derek McInnes his first point as Rangers manager as they fought back for a 1-1 draw againstDundee United.Lachlan Rose struck the first goal of the Premiership season to give United a half-time lead at Tannadice.Scottish Premiership returns with McInnes adding new twist to Old Firm rivalryRead moreRangers lacked control in possession in the opening period but they looked more threatening after the break and Aasgaard finished brilliantly in the 56th minute. They could not build on the equaliser, though, as United soon stemmed the tide of pressure.Jesse Randall should have won the game for the home side with eight minutes left when substitute Daniel Bennie’s swerving pass put the New Zealand international clean through on goal. However, the winger totally lacked conviction as he dinked a shot straight into goalkeeper Ivor Pandur’s hands.McInnes named Youssef Chermiti on the bench in his first team selection with Ryan Naderi handed a role on the right of Rangers’ attack, and Pandur, Ben Godfrey, Cammy Devlin and Lawrence Shankland making their debuts.There were only two Scots in the two starting lineups but both led their teams, former Falkirk midfielder Dylan Tait wearing the armband for United and Shankland the new Rangers captain.The former Hearts striker was the first to threaten with a flick that drew a reaction stop from Jack Walton, but the home goalkeeper’s only other first-half save came from a Naderi header which looked like it was slightly off target. Rose and Zac Sapsford got in behind for the home side but could not get shots on target and the Rangers defence was busy on other occasions as United worked the ball into the box.View image in fullscreenDerek McInnes began his time at Rangers with a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Dundee United on the opening day of the season.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PADujon Sterling and Mohamed Diomande were off target from outside the box for Rangers, before the hosts made the breakthrough in the 38th minute. Rangers centre-back Emmanuel Fernandez was out of position as Sapsford dummied Randall’s low cross and Rose watched in delight as his left-foot effort spun off the post and over the line.Chermiti and Dan Neil came on for Naderi and Djeidi Gassama as McInnes tried to affect the game at half-time and his side immediately looked more threatening.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideBellingham watches Birmingham beat Barça in friendlyShowJude Bellingham returned to St Andrew's as a spectator to see Birmingham City beat Barcelona on penalties in a pre-season friendly. The England and Real Madrid midfielder (pictured) emerged from Birmingham's academy, making his first-team debut at 16 years old before joining Borussia Dortmund in 2020.August Priske put Birmingham ahead in the 31st minute, but teenage Barça striker Hamza Abdelkarim levelled from the penalty spot before half-time. Abdelkarim struck again on the hour, reacting fastest after Roony Bardghji's shot was saved. Jhon Solis responded for the hosts, volleying home in the 68th minute.The game ended 2-2 after 90 minutes, with Birmingham keeper James Beadle saving twice and 17-year-old Barcelona defender Jordi hitting the crossbar. The shootout ended 3-2 to Birmingham as the hosts enjoyed a memorable victory over an admittedly inexperienced Barcelona line-up.Guardian sportPhotograph: Nigel French/PAWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Aasgaard forced an excellent diving save from Walton before the Norway international levelled moments later. Shankland’s physical presence caused problems as United were made to defend another high ball and Aasgaard took an excellent touch to take out Joshua Rawlins before firing a left-foot strike into the top corner from 16 yards.Rangers could not keep up the momentum, and Randall squandered a glorious chance to mark his league debut with a famous winner. Chermiti almost made the home side pay but Walton stopped the striker’s effort with his feet before home substitute Idjessi Metsoko delivered a weak effort straight at Pandur from a decent opportunity.Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipDundee UnitedRangersmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Franco Baresi was not only the captain but the moral heart of great Milan team | Milan | The Guardian
description: The centre-back, who has died aged 66, defined an era of hard Italian defending and his collection of honours is eternal proof of his class
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: The centre-back, who has died aged 66, defined an era of hard Italian defending and his collection of honours is eternal proof of his class
Content: Franco Baresi was calm personified as he marshalled defence and looked for a pass to a teammate.Photograph: Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenFranco Baresi was calm personified as he marshalled defence and looked for a pass to a teammate.Photograph: Action Images/ReutersMilanFranco Baresi was not only the captain but the moral heart of great Milan teamThe late centre-back defined an era of Italian defending and his collection of honours is eternal proof of his classJonathan WilsonFri 31 Jul 2026 08.20 EDTLast modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere are very few players who become bywords for their position, who enjoy universal acclaim. But for anybody who watched football in the late 80s or early 90s, Franco Baresi wasthecentral defender. He was unsurpassed, obviously the best in his position in the world, the definition of the art of the defending. The oddity is, he really wasn’t like very many other defenders at all.Baresi had just turned 19 when he won his firstscudettoatMilanunder Nils Liedholm. It was 1979 and Italian football was still dominated by the ideals ofcatenaccio. Most defences comprised a libero, two man-markers and, if you were lucky, an attacking left-back. But not Liedholm’s. The Swede was a pioneer in Serie A of zonal marking, and the idea that the game was not a series of physical battles but a question of space. Baresi was only 5ft 9in and a teenager. More traditional coaches might not have trusted him. But Liedholm saw an impeccable reader of the game, even at that age. Baresi was an ever-present, not only in the league but in the Coppa Italia and Uefa Cup as well.Franco Baresi, iconic Milan and Italy legend, dies aged 66Read moreThat turned out to be a traumatic season for the club, with players arrested on the pitch after the final game of the season as part of theTotonerobetting scandal, for which Milan were ultimately relegated. With the club in financial chaos, promotion was followed by another relegation and, although they were promoted again, the future seemed bleak before Silvio Berlusconi took over in 1986. Baresi remained loyal throughout. His parents died before he turned 16 and Milan became a sort of surrogate family.He never played for any other club, amassing 719 appearances in all competitions over 20 years. And yet, he could easily have been an Inter player. Baresi’s brother Giuseppe, two years his elder, was already at Inter when Franco was offered a trial at the age of 14. Inter wondered if he was big enough to make it and asked him to come back the following year. So Franco went for a trial at Milan – which he insisted had always been his club – and was taken on.Berlusconi was an outsider, determined to disrupt the establishment. In Arrigo Sacchi, who was appointed in 1987, he found a coach in the same vein: a radical who followed Liedholm’s tentative steps into the world of zonal marking with a giant leap into a full-blown flat back four and hard pressing. In the Serie A of the age it was almost unthinkably revolutionary. Conservatives were sceptical and, when Milan lost their second game of the season 2-0 at home to Fiorentina, and followed that up with defeat to Espanyol in the Uefa Cup and a disappointing draw against Cesena, the joke was that Berlusconi’s new messiah would not make All Saints’ Day, which is 1 November.Form began to turn around, but Sacchi worried he had pushed the players too hard and eased back on training, at which point Baresi made a decisive intervention. He begged Sacchi to push the players even harder. It was vital, he said, that the players didn’t forget, that they came to learn the new way of playing, of working out their position not according to preset formulas but through constantly evolving reference to opponents, their teammates, the ball and the space, to internalise the processes until they became instinctive.View image in fullscreenFranco Baresi (kneeling, second left) and his Milan teammates celebrate beating Steaua Bucharest 4-0 to win the 1989 European Cup, for many the high point of their football under Arrigo Sacchi.Photograph: PA Images/AlamyFor Sacchi, it was a huge moment. Baresi was not only the captain, but the moral heart of the team. If he was on board with the revolution, Sacchi realised, the squad would follow. Milan, with their ultra-modern style, won thescudettoin 1988 and backed it up with consecutive European Cup wins, playing some of the most memorable football ever witnessed. Baresi was central to it, not only snuffing out opposing forwards but constantly analysing and organising, and also initiating counterattacks. The clipped forward pass became a trademark, but his greatest skill was his pass selection. He just didn’t give the ball away.His inspirations were creative players plus Ruud Krol, but Baresi was also tough. Gianfranco Zola called him the best defender he ever played against but observed that afterwards “your feet need loads of ice and anti‑inflammatories”. Baresi dished it out, as defenders in Serie A in those days had to, but he could also take it. He played more than an hour of a Milan derby in 1989 with a broken arm, helping keep a clean sheet, and, at the 1994 World Cup, managed to recover from knee surgery required after tearing his cartilage in the second group game in time to play in the final. Again, he oversaw a clean sheet but, cruelly, failed from the spot in the shootout asItalylost to Brazil.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenA Milan fan lays flowers next to a shirt of former captain Franco Baresi at Casa Milan.Photograph: Daniele Mascolo/ReutersInternational football never quite gave Baresi the highs the club game did. He was part of the World Cup-winning squad in 1982 but didn’t play a minute, and was part of squads that got to the last four of Euro 88 and Italia 90, but he never achieved the same glory with Italy that he did with Milan.And so the memory of him will always be in the red-and-black shirt, anticipating the game, stepping implacably in front of an opponent, shrugging him off and clipping a perfectly weighted ball in to a forward’s feet, the defining image of Italy’s new era of defending.Explore more on these topicsMilanItalyFootball tacticsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Chelsea fined £10m and given suspended transfer ban by FA over agent breaches | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: The club escaped a suspended six-point deduction for the infringements after appealing against the original punishment
Author: Paul MacInnes
Headline: The club escaped a suspended six-point deduction for the infringements after appealing against the original punishment
Content: Chelsea have been fined £10m and given a suspended two-window transfer ban after admitting breaches of agent rules.Photograph: JP Fletcher/Action Plus/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenChelsea have been fined £10m and given a suspended two-window transfer ban after admitting breaches of agent rules.Photograph: JP Fletcher/Action Plus/ShutterstockChelseaChelsea fined £10m and given suspended transfer ban by FA over agent breachesClub escape suspended six-point deduction on appealOwners admitted secret payments by previous regimePaul MacInnesandRob DaviesFri 31 Jul 2026 09.55 EDTLast modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 15.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea have been fined £10m by the FA and served with a suspended transfer ban for multiple violations of transfer rules during theRoman Abramovichera.The sanction reflects a similar punishment handed to the Blues by the Premier League earlier this year after the club were found to have used unlicensed agents and sought to obscure the nature of their transfer dealings between 2009 and 2022. Deals involvingChelsealegends Samuel Eto’o, Eden Hazard and Willian were among those found to have breached the rules. The commission originally handed down a stronger sanction that would have given Chelsea a suspended six-point deduction, but it was overturned after an appeal by the club.Chelsea fined £10.75m and given suspended transfer ban over historical rule-breakingRead moreThe offences were self-reported by Chelsea when new ownership entered Stamford Bridge in 2022 and the disciplinary panel praised the club for their actions and cooperation through the hearing. Chelsea, who are also operating under a settlement agreement with Uefa, said they had “worked openly and transparently with all regulators” and were “pleased to confirm that this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close”.Written reasons published by the FA show the independent commission took a very dim view of the Abramovich-era administration, saying their rule-breaking showed “a shameful and arrogant disregard for the rules of the game … which has done so much to bring the game of football in general, and the name of CFC into disrepute”. They also said, however, that there were aspects of the case brought by the FA that caused them “particular concern”.While praising the FA’s cooperation on the case, the commission criticised the governing body for both failing to charge individuals related to the misdemeanours and for requesting that a sporting sanction should not be applied as punishment. After a submission by the Premier League, which also argued against a sporting sanction, Chelsea appealed against the commission’s original sanction and the six-point deduction was replaced with a suspended two-window ban on registering new players. While the commission had originally argued Chelsea had sought and gained a sporting advantage from their actions, the appeal board found that there was insufficient evidence to show that any advantage had actually been achieved.“Chelsea’s lawyers performed a masterclass in non-adversarial diplomacy with both the FA and the Premier League,” said Stefan Borson, a football finance expert who is head of sport at the law firm McCarthy Denning.“Even where the FA’s independent panel disagreed with the position presented by the FA and Chelsea, it still found a way to discount a 15-point deduction starting point down to a six-point suspended penalty. Ultimately, even that was appealed away, leaving Chelsea to pay a final meagre fine out of its retained escrow from Abramovich’s proceeds.”Quick GuideMudryk cleared to resume playingShowChelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk can return to playing immediately after the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency “resolved his appeal” against a ban for failing a doping test.The Ukrainian was suspended for four years after failing a drug test which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, in 2024. Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport while changes to Wada procedures in the interim mean that had his failed test produced the same result now, charges would not have been brought.The FA said: “Changes have been made … which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk’s sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations [ADRVs] would have resulted. Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now – with the agreement of Wada – resolved the appeal proceedings.“As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the ADRVs charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect.”PA MediaWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The Premier League and the FA had been examining tens of millions of pounds in secret payments made by offshore companies that were owned by Abramovich. Details of the transactions were uncoveredas part of Cyprus Confidential, an investigation by the Guardian and international media partners, based on a leak of data from Cypriot financial services firms that the Russian oligarch used to manage his vast fortunes.Deals revealed by the leak included apparent off-book payments to Hazard’s agent and an associate of the title-winning manager Antonio Conte.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDocuments published as part of the finding offer a rare insight into the inner workings of Chelsea’s transfer policy during the tenure of Abramovich. They refer to internal conversations at Chelsea about the purchase of Willian in 2013, a deal agreed at the last minute, after the Brazilian had apparently been set to join London rivals Tottenham. According to the documents, an unnamed senior figure at Chelsea felt that to lose Willian was “not good” and that to lose him to Tottenham was “adding insult to injury”.In its argument, the FA said the unnamed individual may have “loved the power associated with having a bottomless pocket when it came to acquiring players of great quality and/or with great potential, but to seek to suggest that there was no intention to obtain a sporting advantage is stretching our credulity beyond reasonable limits”.The rulings published by the FA also reveal for the first time that BlueCo, the consortium that bought Chelsea from Abramovich, reached a multi-million pound settlement with HM Revenue & Customs relating to transactions dating back to 2011. The size of the settlement is redacted in the FA’s case against Chelsea but the appeal board’s decision indicated that the club repaid at least £1.35m.The FA said that the entirety of Chelsea’s £10m fine will be invested into grassroots football.Explore more on these topicsChelseaThe FARoman AbramovichnewsShareReuse this content

title: Arsenal target Bruno Guimarães not on Newcastle’s flight to pre-season camp | Newcastle United | The Guardian
description: The midfielder was absent as teammates head to La Manga, as Eddie Howe confirms he has stood down as head coach ‘to recharge and take a break’.
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: The midfielder was absent as teammates head to La Manga, as Eddie Howe confirms he has stood down as head coach ‘to recharge and take a break’.
Content: Newcastle fans’ last sighting of Bruno Guimarães was in Brazil’s last-16 defeat against Norway in the World Cup.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/SportsphotoView image in fullscreenNewcastle fans’ last sighting of Bruno Guimarães was in Brazil’s last-16 defeat against Norway in the World Cup.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/SportsphotoNewcastle UnitedArsenal target Bruno Guimarães not on Newcastle’s flight to pre-season campMidfielder could still fly to La Manga on SundayHowe says he stood down ‘to recharge and take a break’Louise TaylorFri 31 Jul 2026 12.17 EDTFirst published on Fri 31 Jul 2026 08.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBruno Guimarães was not on Newcastle’s flight to Murcia on Friday lunchtime as Eddie Howe’s former players prepared to meet their new head coach in southern Spain.As Guimarães, who is believed to be in Brazil, appeared to inch closer towards a transfer toArsenal, Matthias Jaissle was completing his managerial move from Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli. Howe’s successor is expected to arrive at the club’s pre-season training camp at La Manga at some point this weekend.Not so black and white: how Eddie Howe lost control at Newcastle in one summer | Louise TaylorRead moreBy the time, shortly after midday, when the team’s charter plane took off for the Mediterranean, Newcastle had still to provide formal confirmation of Howe’s departure. That did not arrive until late afternoon but it is understood they had been negotiating a financial settlement with their former manager in addition to payoffs for four key members of his backroom staff, including the outgoing No 2, Jason Tindall.In an emotional message released as part of Newcastle’s statement, Howe said. “It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager ofNewcastle United. After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into this club with unrelenting energy I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break. Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart it’s the right one.”The amicable nature of the parting was reflected in generous tributes paid by Newcastle’s chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson and minority owner, Jamie Reuben. The latter said: “I am proud to have worked alongside Eddie Howe and privileged to call him a friend.” Hopkinson said: “Eddie and his staff leave with the deep gratitude and respect of everyone at Newcastle United and a lasting place in the club’s history.”Although Howe had told Newcastle of his intention to leave earlier this month, leaks surrounding Jaissle’s imminent installation appeared to catch all parties by surprise. The players had learned of their manager’s departure during a day off on Thursday but had the situation fully explained when Wilson addressed them at the training ground before heading to Spain alongside the squad.At the same time, Newcastle’s incoming German head coach was understood to be finalising a four-year contract at St James’ Park after an £8m compensation package was agreed with Al-Ahli. Jaissle is already in Europe after remaining in Portugal rather than returning to Jeddah with his squad following the conclusion of a pre-season training camp on the Algarve on Wednesday.View image in fullscreenJoelinton could be on his way to the Saudi Arabia league this summer.Photograph: Siu Wu/EPAThe 38-year-old former RB Salzburg manager is assembling his own backroom staff and now has only three weeks before his first Premier League season begins with a home game against Liverpool.One of his first tasks will be to hold talks with Guimarães regarding the Brazil midfielder’s future. Guimarães – who was very close to Howe – is booked on a flight to Spain on Sunday but there are suggestions he could opt to board a London-bound plane instead, should Arsenal offer Newcastle a sum in the region of £75m.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAlthough Manchester United are exploring the possibility of signing Lewis Hall, Jaissle has reason to be more confident of keeping the influential left back. Newcastle are said to be determined to retain one of their best young players but could be more receptive to any bid from Saudi Arabia for Joelinton. Guimarães’s fellow Brazilian is believed to be keen on a move to the Middle East.While Besiktas also covet another Newcastle midfielder, Joe Willock, Wilson appears close to securing a new goalkeeper. A £26m deal for the Braga and Czechia goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek is expected to be completed over the weekend.Should that move for the 24-year-old progress as planned, Nick Pope, Newcastle’s current first-choice keeper, will almost certainly prove yet another departure during a turbulent summer featuring a major changing of the guard on Tyneside.Explore more on these topicsNewcastle UnitedArsenalEddie HowenewsShareReuse this content

title: Who should win the men’s Ballon d’Or? | Ballon d'Or | The Guardian
description: Harry Kane, Rodri, Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi are the frontrunners for the annual prize
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Harry Kane, Rodri, Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi are the frontrunners for the annual prize
Content: Harry Kane, Rodri and Lamine Yamal are in contention for the annual prize.Composite: Guardian Pictures; Reuters; Copa/Getty Images; EPAView image in fullscreenHarry Kane, Rodri and Lamine Yamal are in contention for the annual prize.Composite: Guardian Pictures; Reuters; Copa/Getty Images; EPAGuardian Sport NetworkBallon d'OrWho should win the men’s Ballon d’Or?Harry Kane, Rodri, Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi are the frontrunners for the annual prizeByWhoScoredHarry PatersonFri 31 Jul 2026 07.24 EDTLast modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 07.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHarry KaneSeventy-three goals in 64 games for club and country – the second most prolific season by any player in history after Lionel Messi’s 82-goal campaign in 2011-12 – not bad for a man who once sat on the bench alongside Jamie Vardy in the Championship. Harry Kane was not a teenage prodigy like a few of the other players on this list but here he is crashing football’s top table at the age of 33.It feels strange that a player who has scored at least 24 goals in each of the last 12 seasons, has won back-to-back Golden Boots in the Premier League, aWorld CupGolden Boot and two European Golden Shoes, has never finished higher than 10th in Ballon d’Or voting.The numbers were always there but now he is adding the silverware. Kane’s trophy drought ended when Bayern Munich won the Bundesliga last year and that triumph has opened the floodgates. Another Bundesliga title followed this season, alongside the DFB-Pokal and German Supercup.England did not end their trophy drought at the World Cup but their captain scored six goals and overtook Gary Lineker as England’s top scorer at the tournament, ensuring he remained in contention for the Ballon d’Or.Lamine Yamal“It’s about being calm. When I’m in the area with the ball, I decide what happens,” said Lamine Yamal in February after he had scoredthe first hat-trick of his careerin Barcelona’s 4-1 win against Villarreal. For most 19-year-olds this would sound like arrogance, but Yamal is not like most 19-year-olds.He offered more proof of that this summer. The Spain forward became the first player to appear in a European Championship final and a World Cup final before turning 20 – and he won both. He only scored one goal at the World Cup, which was a modest return by his own lofty standards, but he was influential throughout. He won a gamechanging penalty in thesemi-final against France, he made more successful take-ons than Messi across the tournament, and he had a hand in breaking down an Argentina side hellbent on baiting him into a physical duel in the final. He achieved all this after going into the tournament with a hamstring injury. Joe Hart captured the mood best after the final, saying: “Lamine Yamal is 19 years old. What a beautiful day for him. He’s 19 and has completed football.”Add in the 24 goals and 18 assists he racked up in 45 appearances for Barcelona as they won La Liga and the Supercopa, and he has a strong case to go one better than his runners-up finish inlast year’s Ballon d’Or.Rodri“We’ll see the real Rodri at the World Cup,” said Pep Guardiola last October, when the Manchester City captain returned to action after suffering an ACL injury. There were doubts that the 2023 Ballon d’Or winner would ever return to his best. But, as with most things in football, Guardiola was right.World Cup, Ballon d’Or, Champions League, Euros … has Rodri completed football? | The KnowledgeRead moreRodri was the heartbeat and the safety blanket in the Spain team, dictating every phase of the game, controlling possession and extinguishing almost every danger posed to his backline – Spain only conceded one goal in their eight matches at the tournament. Rodri completed 756 passes (more than anyone at the tournament) and he also topped the charts for touches, line-breaking passes and passes in the opposition third. In the final alone he completed 101 passes, completely strangling the life out of Argentina to the extent that they did not have a single shot on target.He lifted the trophy as Spain’s captain, won the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player and earned a place in one of football’s most exclusive clubs as only the fourth man in history to have won the World Cup, European Championship, European Cup and Ballon d’Or, joining Gerd Müller, Franz Beckenbauer and Zinedine Zidane.Kylian MbappéKylian Mbappé went toe-to-toe with his old Paris Saint-Germain teammate Lionel Messi at the World Cup. They battled it out for the trophy, the Golden Boot, the Golden Ball and a place in the history books as the competition’s all-time leading scorer. He won two of the four. His two goals in the third-place playoff against England ensured he became the first man to win the Golden Boot twice. It also brought him to 22 goals in World Cups – one more than Messi – and made him the first man to reach double figures in a single edition since Müller in 1970.And yet, it was not what Mbappé wanted. “I would have preferred not to be the top scorer and to have played in the final,” said the France captain. His domestic season was also prolific but disappointing, bringing goals and individual glory but no silverware. He scored 42 goals in 44 appearances, finishing the season as the top scorer in La Liga and the Champions League, but he did not win either trophy. The goals flowed but the medals did not follow. As Kane has discovered, goals alone are rarely enough to win the Ballon d’Or.View image in fullscreenKylian Mbappé has scored 22 goals in 22 matches at World Cups.Photograph: Carlos Barría/ReutersLionel MessiLionel Messi sat on the floor alone in a stadium of 80,000 people, boots off, staring into the distance as Spain’s substitutes streamed past him in celebration. It was not the fairytale image the Argentina captain had envisioned as he left the world stage. And, given his performances over the previous six weeks, it felt as if he deserved better even if his team did not.Some expected Messi’s tournament to be a nostalgia act – a former great wheeled out for one last World Cup as he prepares for his 40th birthday. But then he went and scoreda hat-trick in Argentina’s first game. He scored twice against Austria, then added another against Jordan. He stamped his authority on the tournament in the group stage and proceeded to drag Argentina through the knockouts:a goal against Cape Verde, a goal and an assistagainst Egypt, an assistagainst Switzerland, and two more assists to sinkEngland in the semi-final. Had it not been for Mbappé’s brace in a bizarre third-place playoff, he would have collected the Golden Boot.Could he win the Ballon d’Or having lost the World Cup final? In only four of the last 19 years has the award gone to a player who did not win the Champions League, World Cup, European Championship or Copa América in the same year. But three of them were won by Messi. A ninth Ballon d’Or is unlikely but the fact he is in this conversation at all – at 39 while playing in MLS having lost a final – is testament to his greatness.This is an article byWhoScoredExplore more on these topicsBallon d'OrGuardian Sport NetworkHarry KaneKylian MbappéLionel MessiWorld Cup 2026World CupfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Jaissle heads for Newcastle after success in Saudi Arabia that has eluded so many | Newcastle United | The Guardian
description: German coach was almost unknown on arrival in Saudi Pro League in 2023 but clinched major titles and won over fans
Author: John Duerden
Headline: German coach was almost unknown on arrival in Saudi Pro League in 2023 but clinched major titles and won over fans
Content: Matthias Jaissle won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before arriving at Al Ahli in summer 2023.Photograph: ReutersView image in fullscreenMatthias Jaissle won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before arriving at Al Ahli in summer 2023.Photograph: ReutersNewcastle UnitedJaissle heads for Newcastle after success in Saudi Arabia that has eluded so manyGerman coach was almost unknown on arrival in Saudi Pro League in 2023 but clinched major titles and won over fansJohn DuerdenFri 31 Jul 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 07.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTaking over a big, underachieving port city club with a loyal fanbase that is desperate for success should not faze Matthias Jaissle. Shouldhe take the role vacated by Eddie Howe, the 38-year-old German will leave Jeddah as a hero and arrive in the north-east as one of the most successful coaches in the history of Asian football.A decade younger than Howe, Jaissle has achieved plenty, not only surviving in a Saudi Pro League that chews through coaches at a rapid rate but emerging victorious. It also helps thatAl-Ahliand Newcastle share the same Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) owners.Eddie Howe leaves Newcastle United with Matthias Jaissle set to replace himRead moreNewcastle fans may know little about the former centre-back, whose playing career was cut short by injury, but that was also the case in Saudi Arabia when he arrived three years ago. Austria’s Bundesliga is not followed much in Asia, so two titles won with Red Bull Salzburg did not mean a great deal: neither did Jaissle’s association with Ralf Rangnick.Fans were more focused on Al-Ahli’s recent return to the top flight, after a first season in the second tier, and were contemplating an influx of big-name players. A little different to the situation at St James’ Park with stars such asSandro TonaliandAnthony Gordonalready gone and others seemingly about to follow.In Jeddah, Riyad Mahrez, Roberto Firmino, Édouard Mendy, Franck Kessié and others arrived in a summer when the club was acquired by PIF. For a team that had been in the doldrums a year earlier, it was quite a turnaround.Despite all that Al-Ahli may have been the perfect club for Jaissle. The fans are famously passionate but had only one domestic league win since 1984. In Asia there had been two comprehensive Champions League final defeats. Compared to Al-Hilal, Al-Nassr and Al-Ittihad – also in the PIF stable – the Green corner of Jeddah had been relatively starved of success and, for a while, challenging again was enough.For the then 35-year-old, dealing with such names did not seem a problem. His straight-talking style, with the foreign stars treated the same as the locals, drew a positive response. With his wealth of attacking talent Jaissle tried to win possession as high as possible to give players such as Mahrez the chance to shine. His preferred attack-minded, high-intensity playing style may move up a gear by the North Sea compared to the heat and humidity of the Red Sea.View image in fullscreenGaleno (right) was a key signing for Al-Ahli under Jaissle and brought the best out of Ivan Toney in attack.Photograph: ReutersIn his first season Al-Ahli finished third, 11 points ahead of their fierce local rivals Al-Ittihad and, crucially, qualified for the AFC Champions League Elite. The second season was more difficult, for a while at least. After the departure of Allan Saint-Maximin, Jaissle wanted a replacement winger but, instead, Ivan Toney was signed and the England striker started slowly. Results dipped but were improving by January 2025 when the axe threatened to fall. Max Allegri was ready to take over, the kind of eye-catching coach that fans often want. But not in this case – members of the Green Army supported Jaissle, who had always taken time out to praise and talk to fans. A group of them appeared at the training ground with banners telling club management they should be the ones to go.And it worked. Al-Ahli said Jaissle was staying with their full support. In came a winger, Galeno from Porto, and with the Brazilian getting the best out of Toney, Al-Ahli moved up a gear. They finished fifth in Jaissle’s second season but got more points. It was all about the Champions League, however. In the semi-finals, they defeated Al-Hilal, 19-time Saudi and four-time Asian winners. Then, in May 2025, in front of 60,000 fans in Jeddah, Kawasaki Frontale of Japan were defeated.Then Al-Ahli did it again, winning the Asian title for a second time last May to become the first team since their Jeddah rivals, Al-Ittihad (in 2004 and 2005), to clinch successive Champions League crowns.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThey also had a title challenge at home that only faded in the final weeks with Toney scoring 32 goals. In 34 games the team collected 81 points, 14 more than the previous season, and had Al-Nassr and Al-Hilal not been so consistent then it could have been a spectacular double.The focus for the new season, due to start in August, was all about the Saudi Pro League title; but that should be someone else’s concern now.Jaissle was recently linked with Al-Hilal and while that wouldn’t have gone down well with fans in Jeddah, he heads to Newcastle with the blessing of most. The German was always likely to return to Europe, and departs with success in Saudi Arabia, having won major titles. Many more experienced coaches have failed in that regard. Newcastle will be a different and tougher challenge.He is not part of the elite any more but taking Newcastle closer to the Premier League’s top four would be a good start.Explore more on these topicsNewcastle UnitedAl-AhlifeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Isaac Beacroft walks to gold on mixed day for Australia at Commonwealth Games | Commonwealth Games 2026 | The Guardian
description: The teenage race walker held off Stephen Kihu over 10,000m but there was disappointment for Nina Kennedy, Torrie Lewis and Lachie Kennedy
Author: Jack Snape
Headline: The teenage race walker held off Stephen Kihu over 10,000m but there was disappointment for Nina Kennedy, Torrie Lewis and Lachie Kennedy
Content: Australian race walker Isaac Beacroft wins the men's 10,000m race walk final at Scotstoun Stadium in Glasgow.Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAPView image in fullscreenAustralian race walker Isaac Beacroft wins the men's 10,000m race walk final at Scotstoun Stadium in Glasgow.Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAPCommonwealth Games 2026Isaac Beacroft walks to gold on mixed day for Australia at Commonwealth GamesSarah Billings claims Australia’s first 800m women’s bronze in 36 yearsBut disappointment for three other track and field stars in GlasgowJack SnapeFri 31 Jul 2026 19.08 EDTLast modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 19.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTeenage race walker Isaac Beacroft hit the accelerator on a dramatic final lap in the 10,000m then had to hit it again, celebratingCommonwealth Gamesgold 20 metres before the finish despite his Kenyan rival Stephen Kihu lurking just a few steps behind.The result was the Australian highlight on a mixed day at Scotstoun Stadium in Glasgow, as Sarah Billings claimed her country’s first 800m women’s bronze in 36 years, even as track and field stars Nina Kennedy, Torrie Lewis and Lachie Kennedy were left disappointed.Australia’s Georgia Baker joins select cycling club with fifth Commonwealth Games goldRead moreBeacroft, the under-20 world record holder, stormed away from Kihu with 300m to go to secure gold. “Probably the last 15 laps, I was just waiting for Kihu to go, but he never did, so I sat in, and eventually had to go,” he told Channel Seven. “I went hard, about 95%, and then I knew he was going to come with me, but then I had another gear in there to really make it over.”He secured the breakthrough win, but not without fraying the nerves of his father and coach David. “He’s having a panic,” Beacroft told Channel Seven with a smile. “He thought I was going to get chased down, and started celebrating too early. Rubbish.”Beacroft Sr, a former race walker himself, admitted he might have done things differently. “I just saw the guy make another surge and I’m like, ‘Oh, don’t do too much too soon’, but he held him off. It was nice, it was good, really good.”The 19-year-old, whose celebrations and interviews in Glasgow marked the birth of a new showman in Australian athletics, now heads to Oregon to compete at the world juniors in just nine days.View image in fullscreenAustralia’s 800m bronze medallist Sarah Billings.Photograph: Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty ImagesBillings’ historic bronze was a mix of brain and braun, as she positioned herself well with a lap to go and pushed all the way up the final straight. The Australian finished behindEnglish winner Georgia Hunter Belland Kenyan Lilian Odira, last year’s world champion who Billings almost beat at the line.While that bronze medal provided unbridled joy for Billings, a silver in the pole vault for Nina Kennedy left the Paris Olympic champion with mixed emotions. “If you don’t laugh, you’ll cry,” she said. “So I’m trying to put on a happy face right now, but look, I’m disappointed. I wanted the gold.”In blustery conditions she cleared 4.65m but finished second on a count-back to Eliza McCartney, who won New Zealand’s second track and field gold at these Games after Zoe Hobbs’s 100m success.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenNina Kennedy with her silver medal.Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAPLewis, who finished third behind Hobbs in that 100m final two days ago, ran gallantly to finish sixth in the final of the 200m, won by Adaejah Hodge of the British Virgin Islands. “Not what I wanted for the 200,” Lewis said. “I made the final which was one of my goals so I’m still proud of that, and I look towards the relay.”Echoes of 1954 as Kerr, Wightman and rising star Myers face off in mile raceRead moreIn the men’s 200m, Lachie Kennedy also finished sixth. The 100m silver medallist and new 9.85sec man started well but faded behind South African winner Sinesipho Dambile. “I knew if I wanted to win, I was going to have to risk it,” Kennedy said. “Look, I gave it a red hot crack. Didn’t have enough juice in the tank. Credit to the winners. But yeah, I’m gassed.”Like Lewis, Lachie Kennedy will compete in the 4x100m relay on a busy final day of competition in Glasgow, which also includes men’s and women’s mile races. The women’s event is a chance for Jessica Hull to get one back on Claudia Hollingsworth, who caused the Paris silver medallist to fallin a controversial 1500m final at the national championships in April.The men’s event promises to one of the races of these games. It will feature Scottish pair Jake Wightman and Josh Kerr, who broke the men’s world record in the mile last month, as well as reigning Commonwealth champion Olli Hoare and his fellow Australians Adam Spencer and Cam Myers. The latter was described by Wightman this week as“the future of the sport”.Explore more on these topicsCommonwealth Games 2026AthleticsCommonwealth GamesAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Field and French flourish for Wigan to boost title charge with victory at Leigh | Super League | The Guardian
description: Tries from Jai Field and Bevan French sparked Wigan’s 20-8 victory at Leigh to move them up to second in Super League and boost their title credentials
Author: Aaron Bower
Headline: Tries from Jai Field and Bevan French sparked Wigan’s 20-8 victory at Leigh to move them up to second in Super League and boost their title credentials
Content: Bevan French enjoys his try for Wigan in their comeback victory at Leigh.Photograph: Ed Sykes/SWpix.com/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenBevan French enjoys his try for Wigan in their comeback victory at Leigh.Photograph: Ed Sykes/SWpix.com/ShutterstockSuper LeagueField and French flourish for Wigan to boost title charge with victory at LeighSuper League: Leigh 8-20 WiganWigan move up to second within two points of LeedsAaron BowerFri 31 Jul 2026 17.08 EDTLast modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere are moments inSuper Leagueseasons, marathons as they are, which can often prove to be sliding doors occasions for both teams involved. And as the full-time hooter sounded in Leigh and Wigan celebrated another statement win with their travelling support, it was not difficult to imagine how one particular moment from this derby could swing the seasons of both teams.For nearly 40 minutes, Leigh had done something no team had managed to do to Wigan for quite some time: make them appear second best. The Warriors, on a run of nine consecutive wins which began with theirChallenge Cup triumph at Wembleyin May, had been completely outplayed by their local rivals and their own coach admitted they were lucky to be only 8-0 behind.Kitchen magnate finds recipe for Wakefield joy in historic rugby league cityRead moreBut great teams, and great players, find a way to win. Leigh’s first real mistake came two minutes before half-time, when they turned their backs on Jai Field after conceding a penalty, expecting Wigan to kick for touch. Instead, Field tapped the ball and raced 90m downfield to reduce the deficit to just two points by half-time. Just like that, it turned.When Leigh produced another error three minutes after the restart, the Warriors’ other talisman, Bevan French, pounced to inexplicably move Wigan ahead in a game they had been dominated in to that point. Two more Leigh knock-ons followed soon afterwards and once again, the visitors scored tries from both of them.Nobody knows how this would have ended had Leigh led more convincingly at half-time. If the Leopards had won, they would have inserted themselves into the picture for the top two. Instead, they are now sitting sixth and looking nervously over their shoulders. Wigan,meanwhile, march on– they are now second and just two points behind the league leaders, Leeds.Perhaps in a way it was a lesson as to the step Leigh still need to take to compete with a side like Wigan. But the Warriors, frustrated as they will be by the level of this performance, should take great heart from the fact that if they can be this below par with the ball and still win against a playoff rival, imagine what they can do if it clicks in a playoff tie this autumn.View image in fullscreenJai Field dives over for Wigan’s first try of the night in their victory.Photograph: Ed Sykes/SWpix.com/Shutterstock“We needed to improve because in that first half we were second best,” their coach, Matt Peet, said. “We’ve managed our way out of a situation there. There was nothing wrong with our effort but they were very good. You don’t want to win this way every week but it’s good to know it’s in the locker.”Leigh deservedly led by eight points early on thanks to Innes Senior’s outstanding try and two goals from the boot of Adam Cook, but there was no doubting the big moment here – Field’s breakaway try – left a mark on them. The Leopards will hope it does not leave any long-lasting damage in their push to make the playoffs again.“I went in and tried to lift them at half-time but it felt like that moment was a bit of an implosion,” Leigh’s coach, Adrian Lam, said. “It was hard to watch in the second half but we were awesome in that first half. It was unbelievably good, and we are very close to being very good. A bit of negativity crept in and our gameplan just fell apart.”Field’s and French’s tries turned an eight-point deficit into a lead either side of half-time. When Leigh turned possession over cheaply again, Zach Eckersley was the third grateful recipient of a momentary lapse from the Leopards. Then as the hour mark struck, Noah Hodkinson was afforded the same opportunity to make it 20-8 and from there, Wigan were wise enough defensively to close out a crucial win.But this was a captivating and engrossing derby. With the National Rugby League’s bid for control of Super League incoming over the next few days, this was an advert for everything that is great about the competition. A sold-out stadium, a local rivalry and star talent proving to be the difference when it mattered most.Yet for all the change potentially coming Super League’s way off the field, one constant is that it would take a brave man to back against Wigan prevailing at Old Trafford again in October.Explore more on these topicsSuper LeagueLeigh LeopardsWigan WarriorsRugby leaguenewsShareReuse this content

Author: Billy Munday
Headline: England’s Georgia Hunter Bell won the women’s 800m final in style to claim her first Commonwealth Games medal
